El Cabildo de Tenerife presentó hoy (viernes 23) la programación artística de TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes para 2026 e hizo balance de lo acontecido en el museo durante 2025. Acompañados del equipo de TEA, el consejero de Cultura y Museos del Cabildo de Tenerife, José Carlos Acha, y el director artístico de TEA, Sergio Rubira, dieron a conocer las exposiciones que podrán verse este año, que estarán dedicadas a artistas como Cabello/Carceller, Cándido Camacho, Pérez y Requena, Irene Kopelman, Pepa Izquierdo y José Aguiar. También —adelantó Rubira— se celebrará la segunda Bienal Contemporánea TEA, una muestra vinculada a la colección del museo y el fondo de la galería Conca que se centra en el contexto lagunero de los 70 y una gran exposición colectiva articulada a partir de la lectura de algunos textos del antropólogo Fernando Estévez. Además de esta intensa agenda expositiva, que se completará con muestras del MiniTEA y de Óscar Domínguez (artista que tendrá su espacio permanente), TEA incluye una amplia oferta de programas audiovisuales, educativos y públicos que consolidan al museo como un espacio de pensamiento, mediación y creación permanente."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://tenerifeweekly.com/2026/03/27/tea-museum-unveils-four-exhibitions-exploring-contemporary-art-and-avant-garde-legacy-in-the-islands/","title":"TEA Museum Unveils Four Exhibitions Exploring Contemporary Art and Avant-Garde Legacy in the Islands","description":"Letters to Marcelle Ferry’ and ‘Playing’ will be inaugurated this Friday, 27th, at 19:00 hours The TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes will unveil four new exhibitions this Friday at 19:00 hours, showcasing a variety of artistic trajectories ...","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[TEA Museum Unveils Four Exhibitions Exploring Contemporary Art and Avant-Garde Legacy in the Islands]

Letters to Marcelle Ferry, curated by Isidro Hernández; and Playing, held in the revamped MiniTEA Space, realised in collaboration with artists Sema Castro and Elena Galarza."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://tenerifeweekly.com/2026/07/08/the-caam-reopens-its-main-venue-with-two-major-exhibitions-featuring-canarian-painter-juan-jose-gil-and-cuban-artist-sandra-ramos/","title":"The CAAM Reopens Its Main Venue with Two Major Exhibitions Featuring Canarian Painter Juan José Gil and Cuban Artist Sandra Ramos","description":"The Centro Atlántico de Arte Moderno (CAAM) reopens today at 8.00 PM, unveiling two major retrospective exhibitions dedicated to Gran Canarian painter Juan José Gil and Cuban artist Sandra Ramos.","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[The CAAM Reopens Its Main Venue with Two Major Exhibitions Featuring Canarian Painter Juan José Gil and Cuban Artist Sandra Ramos]

The Centro Atlántico de Arte Moderno (CAAM) reopens today at 8.00 PM, unveiling two major retrospective exhibitions dedicated to Gran Canarian painter Juan José Gil and Cuban artist Sandra Ramos. This reopening comes after a ten-month closure for necessary roof renovations.

…

Today, visitors can explore the exhibitions ‘Juan José Gil. Pintura Pintura’ and ‘Sandra Ramos. Soñando otra Ítaca’, which run until October 18, with free entry. These exhibitions continue CAAM’s tradition of showcasing significant artists from the Canary Islands and Latin America, with the latest retrospectives highlighting Gil’s contributions to contemporary art and Ramos’s impact on Cuban and Latin American art.

Gil’s exhibition features 112 works reflecting his exploration of landscape and memory, while Ramos’s display includes around 60 pieces chronicling her artistic journey over the last 30 years, addressing current global complexities through art."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://teatenerife.es/convocatoria/bienal-contemporanea-tea-2026/55","title":"TEA Contemporary Biennial 2026 - TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes","description":"TEA invites artists and collectives ... proposals will be presented in a group exhibition at the museum’s headquarters in November 2026....","relevance":"medium","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Convocatorias > TEA Contemporary Biennial 2026 > Resuelta > Artísticas]

Ever since it first opened, TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes has been firmly committed to artistic experimentation, critical thought and interdisciplinary research. The TEA Contemporary Biennial 2026 is conceived as a space for exploring the relationship between art, territory and community, understanding these concepts not solely as geographic or social categories, but as fields of shared experience, memory and transformation. This edition of the biennial proposes a reflection on territory as a living fabric of relationships, in which art practices act as tools of mediation, care and resistance in the face of contemporary processes of fragmentation and displacement.

The selected projects will seek to activate sustainable bonds between bodies, places and communities, and to foster the emergence of shared spaces of listening and action. TEA invites artists and collectives to apply to this call to develop and present projects whose research and methodology are focused on territory and community, whether through critical reflection, contextual intervention or collaboration with local agents. The processes or results of these proposals will be presented in a group exhibition at the museum’s headquarters in November 2026.

Opening date for call: 2 December 2025

Closing date for call: 2 January 2026.

Acompañados del equipo de TEA, el consejero de Cultura y Museos del Cabildo de Tenerife, José Carlos Acha, y el director artístico de TEA, Sergio Rubira, dieron a conocer las exposiciones que podrán verse este año, que estarán dedicadas a artistas como Cabello/Carceller, Cándido Camacho, Pérez y Requena, Irene Kopelman, Pepa Izquierdo y José Aguiar...

highlights:
[El museo TEA presenta su programación para este año, que incluye una decena de exposiciones > El programa contempla muestras de Cabello/Carceller, Cándido Camacho, Pérez y Requena, Pepa Izquierdo e Irene Kopelman y la celebración de la II Bienal Contemporánea]

El Cabildo de Tenerife presentó hoy (viernes 23) la programación artística de TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes para 2026 e hizo balance de lo acontecido en el museo durante 2025. Acompañados del equipo de TEA, el consejero de Cultura y Museos del Cabildo de Tenerife, José Carlos Acha, y el director artístico de TEA, Sergio Rubira, dieron a conocer las exposiciones que podrán verse este año, que estarán dedicadas a artistas como Cabello/Carceller, Cándido Camacho, Pérez y Requena, Irene Kopelman, Pepa Izquierdo y José Aguiar. También —adelantó Rubira— se celebrará la segunda Bienal Contemporánea TEA, una muestra vinculada a la colección del museo y el fondo de la galería Conca que se centra en el contexto lagunero de los 70 y una gran exposición colectiva articulada a partir de la lectura de algunos textos del antropólogo Fernando Estévez. Además de esta intensa agenda expositiva, que se completará con muestras del MiniTEA y de Óscar Domínguez (artista que tendrá su espacio permanente), TEA incluye una amplia oferta de programas audiovisuales, educativos y públicos que consolidan al museo como un espacio de pensamiento, mediación y creación permanente.

…

The TEA Tenerife Espacio de las Artes will unveil four new exhibitions this Friday at 19:00 hours, showcasing a variety of artistic trajectories and languages. The exhibitions include: Cándido Camacho. Rites of Desire, curated by Alejandro Castañeda and Marta Sesé; So That We Can Live. La Laguna, 1968-1983, curated by the TEA team, coordinated by Néstor Delgado, Vanessa Rosa Serafín, Juan Albarrán, Daniasa Curbelo, and Servando Rocha; Óscar Domínguez. Letters to Marcelle Ferry, curated by Isidro Hernández; and Playing, held in the revamped MiniTEA Space, realised in collaboration with artists Sema Castro and Elena Galarza.

results.title: The CAAM Reopens Its Main Venue with Two Major Exhibitions Featuring Canarian Painter Juan José Gil and Cuban Artist Sandra Ramos
results.description: The Centro Atlántico de Arte Moderno (CAAM) reopens today at 8.00 PM, unveiling two major retrospective exhibitions dedicated to Gran Canarian painter Juan José Gil and Cuban artist Sandra Ramos.

highlights:
[The CAAM Reopens Its Main Venue with Two Major Exhibitions Featuring Canarian Painter Juan José Gil and Cuban Artist Sandra Ramos]

The Centro Atlántico de Arte Moderno (CAAM) reopens today at 8.00 PM, unveiling two major retrospective exhibitions dedicated to Gran Canarian painter Juan José Gil and Cuban artist Sandra Ramos. This reopening comes after a ten-month closure for necessary roof renovations.

…

Today, visitors can explore the exhibitions ‘Juan José Gil. Pintura Pintura’ and ‘Sandra Ramos. Soñando otra Ítaca’, which run until October 18, with free entry. These exhibitions continue CAAM’s tradition of showcasing significant artists from the Canary Islands and Latin America, with the latest retrospectives highlighting Gil’s contributions to contemporary art and Ramos’s impact on Cuban and Latin American art.

Gil’s exhibition features 112 works reflecting his exploration of landscape and memory, while Ramos’s display includes around 60 pieces chronicling her artistic journey over the last 30 years, addressing current global complexities through art.

This edition of the biennial proposes a reflection on territory as a living fabric of relationships, in which art practices act as tools of mediation, care and resistance in the face of contemporary processes of fragmentation and displacement.

The selected projects will seek to activate sustainable bonds between bodies, places and communities, and to foster the emergence of shared spaces of listening and action. TEA invites artists and collectives to apply to this call to develop and present projects whose research and methodology are focused on territory and community, whether through critical reflection, contextual intervention or collaboration with local agents. The processes or results of these proposals will be presented in a group exhibition at the museum’s headquarters in November 2026.
